what_was_actually_wrong: Only 28 of the 30 reported routes were real. The other 2 (GET and PATCH on /workspaces/:workspace_id/loom/views/definitions/:block_id/results) were an artifact of the TEST'S OWN scraper: loom_router_surfaces_from_source ended the last route's method block at end-of-file instead of at the router body, absorbing unrelated get(/patch( tokens from ~4600 lines of handler code below it. Registering those two would have made the manual claim methods the router does not serve and failed mtdoc_every_registry_surface_exists_on_the_real_router with 405.

The named-surface gate only checked backticked spans that were Rust symbol paths (uppercase first char, all alnum/underscore, containing '::'). Routes, env vars, snake_case config keys, hsk.*@N schema ids and bare CamelCase type names all evaded it, and section body_json was never scanned at all.
The storage suite did not run because the three proof commands were &&-chained behind the failing api suite.
